question.text: Mr. Arun Mehra applies for Accredited Investor status. His profile: annual income INR 1.5 crore, net worth INR 6 crore (of which INR 3 crore is financial assets and INR 3 crore is the value of his primary residence). Is he eligible under the Individual AI framework?

answer.text: Yes — annual income of INR 1.5 crore exceeds the INR 1 crore threshold
No — under the combined test, his qualifying net worth is INR 3 crore (excluding primary residence), which is below the INR 5 crore minimum required at the INR 1 crore income level
Yes — total net worth of INR 6 crore alone satisfies the INR 5 crore combined test
No — individual AI threshold is a flat INR 10 crore net worth

explanation.text: The Logic: Individual AI thresholds: (a) annual income ≥ INR 2 crore, OR (b) net worth ≥ INR 7.5 crore (of which ≥ INR 3.75 cr in financial assets), OR (c) annual income ≥ INR 1 crore AND net worth ≥ INR 5 crore (of which ≥ INR 2.5 cr financial assets). Primary residence is EXCLUDED from net worth. Here, Mr. Mehra's qualifying net worth = 6 cr – 3 cr (house) = INR 3 cr, short of the INR 5 cr requirement under the combined test. His income of INR 1.5 cr fails standalone Test-a (need 2 cr). The Trap: Option A misapplies the standalone income test. Option C forgets the primary-residence exclusion — a classic AI framework trap. Option D fabricates a flat INR 10 cr figure. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A, XIX-B Distributor exams test AI onboarding. XXI-B PMS exam uses the same AI framework. X-A/B Investment Adviser exams test the distinction between AI and Qualified Investors. Keep the three tests distinct. Manager's Pro-Tip: Family offices should track both income and net-worth each year. Losing AI status mid-tenure does not unwind past LVF investments (those are grandfathered), but fresh commitments after lapse must be redone under non-AI floor (INR 1 cr min). Set annual AI-recertification calendar with accreditation agency.
